results.name: Connecticut_CAMA_and_Parcel_Layer
results.title: Connecticut CAMA and Parcel Layer
results.description:
Pursuant to Section 7-100l of the Connecticut General Statutes, each municipality is required to transmit a digital parcel file and an accompanying assessor’s database file (known as a CAMA report), to its respective regional council of governments (COG) by May 1 annually. The dataset has combined the Parcels and Computer-Assisted Mass Appraisal (CAMA) data for 2026 into a single dataset. This dataset is designed to make it easier for stakeholders and the GIS community to use and access the information as a geospatial dataset. Included in this dataset are geometries for all 169 municipalities and attribution from the CAMA data for all but one municipality. These data were gathered from the CT municipalities by the COGs and then submitted to CT OPM. This dataset was created on September 2026 from data collected in 2025-2026. Data was processed using Python scripts and ArcGIS Pro for standardization and integration of the data. To learn more about Parcel and CAMA in CT visit our Parcels Page in the Geodata Portal.

Coordinate system: 

This dataset is provided in NAD 83 Connecticut State Plane (2011) (EPSG 6434). Prior versions were provided at  WGS 1984 Web Mercator Auxiliary Sphere (EPSG 3857). 

Ownership Suppression: 

The updated dataset includes parcel data for all towns across the state, with some towns featuring fully suppressed ownership information. In these instances, the owner’s name was replaced with the label "Current Owner," the co-owner’s name will be listed as "Current Co-Owner," and the mailing address will appear as the property address itself. For towns with fully suppressed ownership data, please note that no "Suppression" field was included in the submission to confirm these details and this labeling approach was implemented as the solution.

New Data Fields:

The new dataset introduces the “Property Zip” and “Mailing Zip” fields, which will display the zip codes for the owner and property.

Service URL:

In 2024, we implemented a stable URL to maintain public access to the most up-to-date data layer. Users are strongly encouraged to transition to the new service as soon as possible to ensure uninterrupted workflows. This URL will remain persistent, providing long-term stability for your applications and integrations. Once you’ve transitioned to the new service, no further URL changes will be necessary.

Other Links:

You can also find, download, query and use API resources of this data in the Open Data Portal.

CAMA Notes:

The CAMA underwent several steps to standardize and consolidate the information. Python scripts were used to concatenate fields and create a unique identifier for each entry. The resulting dataset contains 1,354,720 entries and information on property assessments and other relevant attributes.

  • CAMA was provided by the towns.

Spatial Data Notes:

Data processing involved merging the parcels from different municipalities using ArcGIS Pro and Python. The resulting dataset contains 1,282,833 parcels.

  • No alteration has been made to the spatial geometry of the data.

  • Fields that are associated with CAMA data were provided by towns.

  • The data fields that have information from the CAMA were sourced from the towns’ CAMA data.

  • If no field for the parcels was provided for linking back to the CAMA by the town a new field within the original data was selected if it had a match rate above 50%, that joined back to the CAMA.

  • Linking fields were renamed to "Link".

  • All linking fields had a census town code added to the beginning of the value to create a unique identifier per town.

  • Any field that was not town name, Location, Editor, Edit Date, or a field associated back to the CAMA, was not used in the creation of this Dataset.

  • Only the fields related to town name, location, editor, edit date, and link fields associated with the towns’ CAMA were included in the creation of this dataset. Any other field provided in the original data was deleted or not used.

  • Field names for town (Muni, Municipality) were renamed to "Town Name".

Attributes included in the data: 

  • Town Name 

  • Owner

  • Co-Owner

  • Link

  • Editor

  • Edit Date

  • Parcel Collection year

results.title: Connecticut CAMA and Parcel Layer 2024
results.description:
Coordinate system Update:

Notably, this dataset will be provided in NAD 83 Connecticut State Plane  (2011) (EPSG 2234) projection, instead of WGS 1984 Web Mercator Auxiliary Sphere (EPSG 3857) which is the coordinate system of the 2023 dataset and will remain in Connecticut State Plane  moving forward.

Ownership Suppression and Data Access:
The updated dataset now includes parcel data for all towns across the state, with some towns featuring fully suppressed ownership information. In these instances, the owner’s name will be replaced with the label "Current Owner," the co-owner’s name will be listed as "Current Co-Owner," and the mailing address will appear as the property address itself. For towns with suppressed ownership data, users should be aware that there was no "Suppression" field in the submission to verify specific details. This measure was implemented this year to help verify compliance with Suppression.

New Data Fields:
The new dataset introduces the "Land Acres" field, which will display the total acreage for each parcel. This additional field allows for more detailed analysis and better supports planning, zoning, and property valuation tasks. An important new addition is the FIPS code field, which provides the Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) code for each parcel’s corresponding block. This allows users to easily identify which block the parcel is in.

Updated Service URL:
The new parcel service URL includes all the updates mentioned above, such as the improved coordinate system, new data fields, and additional geospatial information. Users are strongly encouraged to transition to the new service as soon as possible to ensure that their workflows remain uninterrupted. The URL for this service will remain persistent moving forward. Once you have transitioned to the new service, the URL will remain constant, ensuring long term stability.

For a limited time, the old service will continue to be available, but it will eventually be retired. Users should plan to switch to the new service well before this cutoff to avoid any disruptions in data access.

results.title: Connecticut Public Use Parcels
results.description:
About this view:

This hosted feature view represents a filtered subset of the statewide parcel and CAMA dataset described below. The subset was produced by executing a text‑based query on the Owner, State Use and State Use Description attributes of the authoritative parcel layer. The query identifies parcels where the fields contains includes text strings associated publicly or privately owned land dedicated to governmental, institutional, infrastructure, utility, transportation, educational, recreational, or other public-serving functions. Data may be missing for certain municipalities (see Ownership Suppression below). 

Publicly Owned Parcels Query:

  • Owner (contains any of the following): state of (exclude “estate”), state of conn, conn state, connecticut historical commission, connecticut airport authority, airport authority, university of conn, city of, town of, united states of america, united states government (us government, u.s. government, u s government), postal serv, post office, passenger co, penn central, board of ed, school dist, connecticut housing finance authority, housing auth, port auth, water auth, water co, sewer auth, public works, or power co. 
  • State Use Description (contains any of the following):  state, fed, gov, post, hosp, fire, pol, library, educ, museum, cemet, mun (muni, munic), util, row, highway, or auth.

This list of search terms is not exhaustive. The GISO has identified minimal false positives with using the above search terms. Reach out at opm.giso@ct.gov with any feedback.

results.title: Vacant Land Viewer
results.description:
Overview 

This map displays land identified as vacant at the parcel level across Connecticut, as described by the CAMA data. It is intended to provide a high-level overview of where these lands are located statewide, serving as a useful general reference. For those developing a Housing Growth Plan under C.G.S. §§ 8-13bb and 8-13cc, this map can help inform the Developable Land Inventory and suitability analysis process. Note that a detailed GIS analysis should still be completed for that purpose, as this map is intended as an overview only. 

Definitions 

  • Vacant Land: This category includes publicly or privately owned land dedicated to governmental, institutional, infrastructure, utility, transportation, educational, recreational, or other public-serving functions that limit or preclude development 

Datasets 

  • Connecticut Vacant Land Parcels: This dataset is derived from the statewide parcel layer maintained by the GIS Office. Parcels were identified as vacant by searching for the parcel attributes for text associated with vacancy. The list of search terms is not exhaustive. While the GIS Office has determined that this method produces minimal false positives and misclassifications, some parcels may still be classified incorrectly.  [See: Connecticut Vacant Parcels] 

Instructions 

To review whether a parcel is designated as a vacant, zoom to your target area. The Vacant Land Parcels and Parcel layers will appear when the map is zoomed in past a zoom scale of less than 1:289,000 and 1:36,000, respectively. Click on a parcel to view the vacant land designation. Use the filters in the top right header bar to query the map by Municipality or Council of Government (COG). Use the filter in the top right of the map to query for specific vacant land parcel types.
results.snippet: This map displays land identified as vacant at the parcel level across Connecticut, as described by the CAMA data.

results.title: Protected Open Space Viewer
results.description:
Overview 

This map displays open space, parks, and recreation areas dedicated to the public or protected by a conservation easement at the parcel level across Connecticut, as described by the CAMA data. It is intended to provide a high-level overview of where these lands are located statewide, serving as a useful general reference. For those developing a Housing Growth Plan under C.G.S. §§ 8-13bb and 8-13cc, this map can help inform the Developable Land Inventory process, specifically the evaluation of the exclusion of land already considered open space as outlined in the Developable Land Inventory Technical Guidance. Note that a detailed GIS analysis should still be completed for that purpose, as this map is intended as an overview only.

Definitions 

  • Protected Open Space: This category includes lands preserved for conservation, passive or active recreation, natural resource protection, or public enjoyment, where development is limited or prohibited by dedication or conservation restriction

 

Datasets 

  • Connecticut Protected Open Space Parcels: This dataset is derived from the statewide parcel layer maintained by the GIS Office. Parcels were identified as open space by searching the parcel attributes for text associated with lands preserved for conservation, passive or active recreation, natural resource protection, or public enjoyment. The list of search terms is not exhaustive. While the GIS Office has determined that this method produces minimal false positives and misclassifications, some parcels may still be classified incorrectly. [See: Connecticut Protected Open Space Parcels]

 

  • DEEP Property: This dataset includes all land owned in fee simple interest by the State of Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection. Types of property in this layer include parks, forests, wildlife areas, flood control areas, scenic preserves, natural areas, historic reserves, DEEP owned waterbodies, water access sites and other miscellaneous properties. [See: DEEP Property]

Instructions 

To review whether a parcel is designated as protected open space, zoom to your target area. The Connecticut Protected Open Space Parcels and DEEP Property layers will appear when the map is zoomed in past a zoom scale of less than 1:289,000 and the Parcel layer will appear when the map is zoomed in past a zoom scale of less than 1:36,000. Click on a parcel to view the protected open space designation. Use the filters in the top right header bar to query the map by Municipality or Council of Government (COG).

results.title: Land Committed to Public Use Viewer
results.description:
Overview 

This map displays lands committed to public use or purpose (public or private) at the parcel level across Connecticut, as described by the CAMA data. It is intended to provide a high-level overview of where these lands are located statewide, serving as a useful general reference. For those developing a Housing Growth Plan under C.G.S. §§ 8-13bb and 8-13cc, this map can help inform the Developable Land Inventory process, specifically the evaluation of the exclusion of land already committed to public use or purpose as outlined in the Developable Land Inventory Technical Guidance. Note that a detailed GIS analysis should still be completed for that purpose, as this map is intended as an overview only. 

Definitions 

  • Land already committed to public use: This category includes publicly or privately owned land dedicated to governmental, institutional, infrastructure, utility, transportation, educational, recreational, or other public-serving functions that limit or preclude development. 

Datasets 

  • Connecticut Public Use Parcels: This dataset is derived from the statewide parcel layer maintained by the GIS Office. Parcels were identified as land committed to public use by searching parcel attributes for text commonly associated with governmental, institutional, or other public-serving ownership or uses. The list of search terms is not exhaustive. While the GIS Office has determined that this method produces minimal false positives and misclassifications, some parcels may still be classified incorrectly. [See: Connecticut Public Use Parcels] 

Instructions 

To review whether a parcel is designated as a land already committed to public use, zoom to your target area. The Public Use Parcels and Parcel layers will appear when the map is zoomed in past a zoom scale of less than 1:289,000 and 1:36,000, respectively. Click on a parcel to view the public use designation. Use the filters in the top right header bar to query the map by Municipality or Council of Government (COG). Use the filter in the top right of the map to query for specific public use parcel types.
